Definition: from G757 and G2994; people-ruling; Archelaus, a Jewish king:--Archelaus.
BiblicalUsage: Archelaus is named once, when Joseph hears that Archelaus reigns in Judaea in the room of his father Herod. Being afraid to go there, Joseph turns aside to Galilee and settles in Nazareth.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe a tyrant's son can change the road a family takes, and God used Joseph's fear of Archelaus to bring Jesus to Nazareth.
RelatedPeople: Archelaus; Herod the Great; Joseph, Husband of Mary
